findings.proposedIrEvidence: The rule records "entityScope": [] and "entityScopeExcluded": []; conditions[0].conditionType is "UNSUPPORTED"; the attempted OR operands are ENTITY_SCOPE_REFERENCE/ENTITY_SET expressions that do not type-check.
findings.verifierReasoning: The entire operative content of §7.2(j) is an entity-scope qualification: the exception is available only for specified debtor/creditor pairs involving Subsidiaries that are not Loan Parties and Subsidiary Guarantors. The proposed IR stores no usable machine-readable entity scope and its only condition is an invalid UNSUPPORTED expression, so a consumer of the IR cannot determine which Indebtedness is permitted. For example, a debt owed by a Loan Party to a non-Loan-Party Subsidiary would be outside the source exception but would not be excluded by the IR as encoded. This can change permission conclusions as to which Indebtedness may be incurred, so it is material. The natural-language semanticDescription is explanatory text, not an evaluable condition, and does not cure the invalid formal expression.

findings.sourceEvidence: Indebtedness of (i) any Subsidiary that is not a Loan Party to any other Subsidiary that is not a Loan Party and (ii) any Subsidiary Guarantor to any Subsidiary that is not a Loan Party;
findings.proposedIrEvidence: The attempted OR operands are bare ENTITY_SCOPE_REFERENCE/ENTITY_SET objects (one with "include": [] and one with "include": ["GUARANTOR_RS"]); neither operand carries a debtor or creditor role.
findings.verifierReasoning: The source creates a directed relationship: the permitted Indebtedness is 'of' a specified debtor 'to' a specified creditor. Clause (i) permits only debts owed by non-Loan-Party Subsidiaries to other non-Loan-Party Subsidiaries; clause (ii) permits only debts owed by Subsidiary Guarantors to non-Loan-Party Subsidiaries. Even if the OR type error were fixed, bare entity-set operands could not distinguish the direction of the obligation. The IR would be unable to distinguish a debt of a Subsidiary Guarantor to a non-Loan-Party Subsidiary (permitted under clause (ii)) from a debt of a non-Loan-Party Subsidiary to a Subsidiary Guarantor (not permitted by either clause). Because that changes the permission conclusion, the missing role structure is material.
